comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized target is the generic 180-EC European Languages and Cultures bachelor. The current official curriculum requires one major language and specialization in one or two of three profiles from Year 2. No profile or major language is substantively more representative of the generic degree. The European Language and Society profile and German major are therefore instantiated through the official-order tie-break: Language and Society is listed first among the profiles, and German is listed first among the major-language options. The pathway preserves the formal 60-EC structure of each year, the 10-EC restricted elective, the 30-EC minor, the 10-EC thesis and every language-specific component without inventing optional content.

routeSelection.route: German major language — European Language and Society profile
routeSelection.basis: The generic programme offers eight major languages and three formal profiles. Current official evidence does not establish one as more representative or more general, so the first-listed profile and first-listed language are selected neutrally, without reference to UCR fit.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Language proficiency, language-and-society analysis, multilingual communication and language-specific academic work
European cultures, identities, literature, text, media and comparative cultural analysis
European politics, institutions, social change and contemporary challenges
adjacent: European language and society through linguistics, rhetoric, media and sociology
European culture and literature through textual and media interpretation
European politics and society through history, political science and sociology
questions: How do language, media and communication shape identity and power in European societies?
How do literature and cultural expression represent similarities and differences across Europe?
How have political institutions and social change shaped modern Europe and its future challenges?

trace: surveys modern European political, economic and cultural change, including nationalism, industrialisation, the world wars, the Cold War and European integration as essential comparative context for modern Europe
introduces sociological concepts and theories for analysing institutions, identity, inequality, migration and social change
studies rhetoric, textual analysis, argument and oral presentation as ways language shapes public meaning
provides the brain, behaviour and research-method foundation required for advanced psycholinguistic study
provides the only explicit European-language acquisition in the UCR catalogue; it is introductory Dutch rather than the comparator’s cumulative German sequence
uses stylistics and literary linguistics to analyse how phonetic, grammatical and discoursal choices create meaning in texts
develops qualitative research design, interviewing and interpretation of situated meanings for research on identity, migration and cultural debate
directly studies European Union institutions, political authority, interests, legitimacy and policy making
examines modernity, imperialism, colonial responses and major sociological debates that shape European social thought
studies film history, form and political context as cultural expression and provides methods for analysing European media without claiming German proficiency
analyses how material media and technologies shape communication, knowledge circulation and cultural memory
applies public speaking, debate and storytelling in a multilingual community setting, supporting intercultural communication without claiming German-language acquisition
analyses memoir, autobiography, diary and travel narratives as culturally situated accounts of identity and encounter
examines identity, conformity, marginalisation and social change through twentieth- and twenty-first-century popular media narratives
analyses documentary representation across historical, social, ethical and aesthetic contexts and develops multimodal production
studies civil society, social trust, public spheres, migrant inclusion and civil repair through contemporary sociological theory
analyses framing, persuasion, ethics and institutional communication in politics, law, media and public organisations
studies how film, photography and music reproduce or resist racial power and how media connect identity, memory and political resistance
uses applied research on radicalisation, democratic school culture and civic engagement to examine a current European social challenge
examines how poetry, performance, voice and experimental media produce culturally situated meaning through critical and creative work
directly studies language acquisition, bilingualism, speech production and comprehension, semantics, and the relationship between language and thought
applies humanist, feminist, Marxist, minority and psychoanalytic perspectives in an advanced text-research project
studies social movements and environmental justice, supporting the evidenced interest in environmental debates and civic mobilisation
establishes practical criticism, genre analysis and literary interpretation for the evidenced literature direction
uses major literary works across historical periods to analyse community, authority, identity and cultural memory
studies empire, great-power politics and competing explanations of imperial rise and decline, supporting historical analysis of Europe
compares literary and oral traditions, cultural transmission and representations of power across languages and regions
develops advanced analysis of literary-to-film adaptation, narration, image, music and sound as forms of cultural expression
examines Western theories of political authority, freedom, equality and pluralism that frame European debates about the state, citizenship and national identity
develops comparative analysis of democratic institutions, parties, backsliding and political participation for studying Germany in European comparison
studies international-relations theories, geopolitics and multilateral negotiation as a framework for Europe’s role in Europe and the international order
develops archival and primary-source historical research through a Napoleonic European case involving German, Dutch, French, British and Polish actors
examines conflict causation, identity-based violence, reconciliation and peacebuilding in regional, national and international settings
traces warfare and military institutions in Western history from antiquity to the present, including the European conflicts central to modern German history
develops evidence-based analysis of misinformation, fake news, cognitive bias and scientific credibility for the evidenced political-culture and public-debate direction

alternatives.label: Language, culture & society in Europe
alternatives.concept: Study language as a social and cultural practice through introductory Dutch, stylistics, psycholinguistics, rhetoric and communication, then connect it to European identity, literature, media, sociology, social change and EU politics. This related-fields route has no German proficiency sequence or German-language academic work.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines seven language and communication courses, literature and media, sociology, European history and EU politics. The label reflects that balance and does not imply German proficiency.
progression: Introductory history, sociology, literature and rhetoric precede advanced communication, psycholinguistics, media and social-theory work. All formal prerequisites and planned terms pass; eight courses are at 300 level.

alternatives.label: Literature, media & cultural identity
alternatives.concept: Study how literary, rhetorical and media forms create cultural meaning and express identity and power, combining textual interpretation, stylistics, psycholinguistics, intercultural communication, film and multimodal production. European and German-language depth remain explicit gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed route concentrates on literature, stylistics, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, film, media and cultural identity; it does not claim German proficiency.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ in each direction. The closest route’s Dutch, EU politics, modern sociology, social movements and applied civic research give way to introductory literary study, major literary traditions, imperial history, myth and advanced adaptation study.
progression: Literature, rhetoric, sociology, brain-and-behaviour and media foundations precede advanced psycholinguistics, literary interpretation, communication and media production. All formal prerequisites and planned terms pass; eight courses are at 300 level.

alternatives.label: Modern Europe, politics & social change
alternatives.concept: Study modern European history, political institutions, international relations, migration, civil society, identity, conflict, environmental movements and public culture as a related social-science and humanities route. Preserve German-language proficiency and language-specific study as explicit gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum is led by European history, politics, international relations, sociology, conflict and public culture and does not present itself as European Languages and Cultures.
alternatives.distinctness: The politics route differs from the closest route by ten courses / 75 EC and from the culture route by ten courses / 75 EC. It replaces Dutch, stylistics, psycholinguistics and much literary/media production with political philosophy, comparative politics, international relations, historical research, conflict and critical-information analysis.
progression: Introductory history, politics and sociology precede international relations, EU politics, advanced historical research, conflict and social theory. All formal prerequisites and planned terms pass; nine courses are at 300 level.

candidates.label: Cumulative European-language proficiency
candidates.assessment: UCR offers one introductory Dutch course but no cumulative proficiency sequence in German or another European language and no language-specific academic curriculum. General psycholinguistics, stylistics and communication cannot be presented as advanced language acquisition.

selection.assessment: Three complete and genuinely different related-fields programmes are defensible: language, culture and society; literature, media and cultural identity; and modern European politics and social change. All three pass the pairwise 30-EC floor. The eight language-direction rows were assessed separately and remain infeasible because UCR lacks cumulative proficiency study; the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

notes.text: Groningen European Languages and Cultures combines cumulative major-language proficiency with language-specific study and one or two formal profiles. UCR can build coherent related programmes in language and society, culture and literature, or European politics and society, but these are not European-language degree pathways.

UCR offers introductory Dutch but no German course and no cumulative proficiency sequence in any European language, language-specific profile modules or thesis in the major language. Psycholinguistics, stylistics, literature, media, history and politics remain related disciplinary perspectives rather than substitutes.

blocks: Both analyse language and society; UCR focuses on stylistics and meaning rather than German proficiency.
Both examine identities through media and culture; UCR is a general media course.
Both develop narrative interpretation and production; UCR focuses on documentary.
Both introduce textual and cultural interpretation.
Both introduce the study of modern Europe; UCR uses historical analysis rather than an integrated programme gateway.
Both develop academic inquiry and qualitative interpretation.
Both examine European institutions and political decision-making.
Both analyse language, culture and society within modern social change; UCR is general sociology.
Both examine society, institutions and public life through advanced theory.
Both examine collective action and contemporary social change.
Both introduce comparative political analysis of European societies.
